title: Birefringent Biomineral Microcarriers Stabilise Multimodal Nanodiamond Quantum Sensing in Liquids
authors: T. Amro, M. Attrash, A. Droby, A. Ushkov, R. Malkinson, P. Penshin, A. Hen, V. Bobrovs, P. Ginzburg, H. Barhum, N. Bar-Gill
abstract: Mobile nanodiamond quantum sensors in liquids are limited by Brownian rotation, variable photon collection, and perturbations introduced by optical trapping. Here, we assemble 40-nm nitrogen-vacancy nanodiamonds at the surface of porous, birefringent vaterite microspherulites. This carbonate biomineral provides a polarization-addressable body frame, anisotropic emission redistribution, and a proton-active thermodynamic interface. Under 976-nm optical trapping, the hybrids retain their spin resonance and longitudinal relaxation, with the resonance contrast varying by less than 7 percent and the resonance centre shifting by approximately 1 MHz at 0.8 W. Zeeman-split resonances enable magnetic-field sensing from 0 to 0.8 mT, with a response metric of 78-144 microT per square root Hz. In buffered cell-culture medium, a 10.7 microM nominal proton-equivalent dose shortens T1 from 23.4 +/- 2.3 to 9.0 +/- 1.2 microseconds, corresponding to concentration and pH sensitivities of 6.46 microM per square root Hz and 6.54 mpH per square root Hz, respectively, in DMEM. By contrast, a 500-fold higher proton dose in ethanol produces a substantially weaker spin response, highlighting the role of the carbonate-rich interface. We develop a grand-canonical charge-regulation model coupling proton chemical potential to interfacial switching kinetics within the NV spectral window, capturing medium-dependent dynamic proton transduction. By integrating orientation stabilisation, optical manipulation, magnetic sensing, and interfacial chemical response, this carbonate-rich hybrid platform establishes a versatile approach to multimodal quantum sensing in complex biological liquids.
summary: The authors engineered a novel quantum sensor by embedding nitrogen-vacancy nanodiamonds onto birefringent biomineral microcarriers. This carrier stabilizes the quantum emitter against liquid motion while providing an active, proton-sensitive interface. The resulting platform enables versatile, multimodal sensing of magnetic fields and chemical species in complex biological media.
main_problem: Liquid nanodiamond quantum sensors are limited by Brownian rotation, variable photon collection, and perturbations from optical trapping, hindering their use as stable probes in complex media.
main_result: By assembling NV centers on birefringent biomineral microcarriers, the system achieves orientation stabilization and demonstrates multimodal sensing (magnetic field and proton/pH) with high sensitivity in liquid environments.
method: The authors combine optical trapping, birefringence-induced torque for mechanical stabilization, ODMR spectroscopy for magnetic measurements, and relaxometry ($T_1$) to probe chemical interactions.
model_or_system: The platform uses 40-nm NV nanodiamonds anchored to porous vaterite microspherulites. The system is modeled using grand canonical charge-regulation models that couple proton chemical potential to interfacial switching kinetics, alongside an effective spin Hamiltonian for optical readout.
key_observables: Zeeman-split resonances (magnetic field sensing), $T_1$ relaxation times ($\mu	ext{s}$ scale), and concentration/pH sensitivities ($\mu	ext{M} \cdot 	ext{Hz}^{-1/2}$, $	ext{mPH} \cdot 	ext{Hz}^{-1/2}$).
important_parameters: Magnetic fields up to $0.8 	ext{ mT}$; proton doses in the range of $10.7 \, \mu	ext{M}$ (DMEM); characteristic relaxation times ($	au_{	ext{match}} \approx 55 	ext{ ps}$).
main_assumptions: The carrier provides an addressable body frame via optical torque, stabilizing the sensor against Brownian motion; chemical sensing relies on modeling the interface as a proton-active thermodynamic boundary.
figures_summary: Figures map the sequence from assembly to readout (optical, Zeeman, chemical); structural evidence confirms NV localization at the carrier–liquid interface; and subsequent figures detail polarization dependence and $T_1$ decay curves under varying conditions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying limitations in free nanodiamonds, then presenting the engineered birefringent carrier platform. It details measurements across magnetic sensing (Zeeman splitting), chemical sensing ($T_1$ in DMEM/ethanol), and concludes with a theoretical model coupling proton chemistry to quantum dynamics.
why_interesting: This work bridges solid-state quantum emitters (NV centers) with complex soft matter interfaces (biomineral carbonates) to create robust, field-deployable sensors. The integration of mechanical stabilization (birefringence) with chemical sensing mechanisms is highly relevant for open quantum systems research.

NV sensing of materials.note: This paper directly utilizes NV centers to probe chemical interactions (pH/proton sensitivity via $T_1$ relaxation) and magnetic fields in a complex liquid environment, which is central to the scope of quantum relaxometry and spin-defect sensing.
